assumptions: The continuous computation of slip ratio from wheel speed and vehicle speed, and the PID controller that produces the slip-error signal, are treated as plant/controller context outside this discrete supervisor DSL. The variable `slp` is modeled as the supervisor input used by the specified transition guards.
The initial state is chosen as `increase` because it is the first state named in the natural-language state list.

transition guards split the slip-error space into four bands: `increase -> hold` when `slp <= 0.01`

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init dispatches to increase with inlet valve command active, then default slp=0.0 satisfies increase->hold and neutralizes valves.
scenario_results.name: default_init_increase_then_default_slip_hold

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start tests that increase transitions to hold exactly at slp=0.01 and applies hold neutral valve outputs.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start tests that increase does not transition to hold when slp is just above 0.01.
scenario_results.name: increase_no_hold_above_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start tests that hold transitions to increase only when slp is strictly greater than 0.01 and applies increase outputs.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_strict_upper_fire

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start tests that hold does not transition to increase at the strict-boundary value slp=0.01.
scenario_results.name: hold_stays_at_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start tests that hold transitions to decrease only when slp is strictly less than -0.01 and applies pressure-release outputs.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_strict_lower_fire

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start tests that hold does not transition to decrease at the strict-boundary value slp=-0.01.
scenario_results.name: hold_stays_at_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes decrease->hold at slp=-0.01 separately from a below-boundary no-fire decrease case.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_boundary_and_below_no_fire

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start tests that decrease does not return to hold while slp remains below -0.01, preserving pressure-release outputs.
scenario_results.name: decrease_stays_below_lower_boundary

evidence: NL states: increase, hold, decrease.
DSL defines state increase, state hold, state decrease.
NL: increase sets k1=1, k2=0, n=0; hold sets k1=0, k2=0, n=0; decrease sets k1=0, k2=1, n=500.
DSL enter actions implement those exact assignments.
NL guards: increase->hold slp <= 0.01; hold->increase slp > 0.01; hold->decrease slp < -0.01; decrease->hold slp >= -0.01.
DSL implements the same four guarded transitions.
findings.summary: The discrete supervisor portion of the DSL closely matches the natural-language FSM: three states, per-state valve/pump assignments, and the four stated slip-error guards are represented directly.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.n_states_leaf = 3.
inspect_model_to_json_summary.transition_count = 5, including one initial transition and four normal guarded transitions.
inspect_model_to_json_summary.action_count = 3.
GroundingMap contains required states, variables, actions, transitions, and guards with high confidence.
findings.summary: Required supervisor components are covered with non-decorative state behavior and executable transition guards.

evidence: NL: wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute the slip ratio, and the PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor.
DSL has only def float slp plus k1, k2, n; there are no wheel speed, vehicle speed, slip-ratio computation, PID state, PID gains, or PID output variables.
GroundingMap.source_summary explicitly assumes continuous computation and PID are outside the discrete supervisor DSL.
findings.summary: The DSL omits the wheel-speed/vehicle-speed slip computation and PID controller mentioned in the NL, modeling only the discrete supervisor input `slp`. This is acceptable for a scoped supervisor model but limits whole-paper coverage.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary.inspect_summary.nl_external_input_vars = ["slp"].
Diagnostic W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR: Variable 'slp' is read but never written.
Diagnostics W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for k1, k2, and n because they are output commands and do not affect guards.
External input role ledger identifies slp as external_input_candidate.
findings.summary: The DSL does not explicitly distinguish external input `slp` from pure outputs `k1`, `k2`, and `n`, causing advisory diagnostics. The role split is inferable from NL and diagnostics metadata, so this is not blocking.

evidence: DSL: [*] -> increase.
GroundingMap.source_summary assumption: initial state is chosen as increase because it is the first state named in the natural-language state list.
NL does not explicitly state the initial state.
findings.summary: The initial state `increase` is an assumption rather than directly specified by the NL. It is plausible but not textually mandated.

evidence: sim_summary.ok = true.
sim_summary.n_scenarios = 9 and n_scenarios_passed = 9.
Scenario names include upper/lower boundary tests, strict fire tests, no-fire tests, and default initialization behavior.
findings.summary: Simulation coverage is adequate for the stated supervisor thresholds, including boundary and strict-inequality cases. Remaining evaluation risk is limited to out-of-scope plant/PID behavior.

evidence: No design blocking diagnostics: design_diagnostics_summary.blocking_count = 0.
Simulation passes all 9 scenarios.
Required supervisor states, guards, and actions are present.
Known limitation: PID and continuous slip computation are treated as external context rather than modeled.
findings.summary: No blocking NFRR quality cap is indicated for the scoped discrete supervisor. Estimated tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate for the supervisor-only interpretation, not a signed whole-paper reference.
